Title: Patrologiae graecae tomus CLX: Gennadius seu Georgius Scholarius, Gregorius Mamma CPolitani patriarchae, alii. Gennadii, Constantinopolitani patriarchae, qui et Georgius Scholarius, Opera omnia, partim jam edita, partim hucusque anecdota. Accedunt Nicolai V Romani pontificis, Gregorii Mammae CPolitani patriarchae, Georgii Gemisti Plethonis, Matthaei Camariotae, Marci Ephesini opuscula et epistolae. Tomus unicus
Creator: Georgios (Gennadios) Scholarios, later Patriarch Gennadios II; Gregory Mammas, patriarch of Constantinople; Mark of Ephesus; Georgios Gemistos Plethon; Matthew Camariotes; Pope Nicholas V; Greek texts with parallel Latin, edited by J.-P. Migne
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne (Petit-Montrouge), Patrologiae cursus completus, Series graeca, tomus 160
Publication Date: 1866
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page's OCR reads '1566' at file line 180, a misreading of the printed year; the list of Migne's volumes in tomus CLXI (file line 110972 of the Bessarion volume vendored beside this one) reads 'CLX (1866). Gregorius Mammas CP., 9-248'. Host record: date field 1857 (the series start), possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item patrologicursus66migngoog (archive.org/details/patrologicursus66migngoog), full-text file patrologicursus66migngoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The OCR text that follows is 6354867 bytes, 4320406 characters and 112514 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 5638, 56270 and 106901): Latin readable with ordinary slips; Greek polytonic readable with chi-for-kappa slips and some garbled lines in the Plethon section.
Content note: Tomus 160 as the volume's own ELENCHUS lists it: Gregory Mammas, patriarch of Constantinople, with his Apology against the confession of Mark of Ephesus (from file line 658); Gennadios Scholarios, the two Confessions of faith written for Sultan Mehmed II (after 1453), his exhortation and orations to the synod at Florence (from file line 31627), his treatises on the procession of the Spirit and on providence and predestination, letters, and fragments on the fall of the City; Georgios Gemistos Plethon (De Peloponnesiacis, fragments of the Laws, against Scholarios's defence of Aristotle); Matthew Camariotes (the Narratio lamentabilis on the fall of Constantinople, from file line 90352); and Mark of Ephesus (notice at 97787, his writings from 98293 and the Addenda at 103878). The Florentine Defensio quinque capitum that circulated under Gennadios's name is not here; the editors give it to Joseph of Methone (tomus 159).

En 1428, Gémistus recut un autre grand hommoge. L'empereur Jean Paléologue, voya- 
geant en Morée, le consulta (3) sur la plus importante affaire politique qui occupát les

toujours croissants de la puissance musulmane, n'attendait plus de secours que du cóté

prix ne pouvait étre débattu que dans un concile. L'empereur avait envoyé des ambassa-
